newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures still down, NY little impact.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures still down, NY little impact.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures continued to drift lower as origins stepped up sales but light manufacturer and trade buying helped slow the descent.

Traders said volume remained fairly modest as most major players, exhausted after a prolonged rally, were sidelined or scaling down their commitment. "The big boys are either out or trading on smaller scale," said one.
Benchmark May finished $30 down at $1,735 a tonne after ranging between $1,728 and $1,765.
Volume totalled 4,608 lots. There was some spread trading in May/Sept which changed hands at $10-$15.
During the day, the London market showed little reaction after New York's arabica futures re-tested the 205.50 cents a lb on May, now seen as a major hurdle.
"We are waiting on the States really. London sitting here, drifting slightly lower and volume is nothing special while people scratch their head to try to figure out what's going on," said one.
New York's May continued its choppy session, trading at between 199 cents and 205.50 and not breaking either way.
Technically the New York market remained bullish although it's a bit overdone.
"I think the market is getting its breath and if it gets above 205.50 and closes above that, we could see more fund and spec buying coming in."
Roaster interest in New York is dying a bit as roasters have either finished their fixings or are awaiting for much lower prices.

With only a week left to go before the spot March contract goes off the board, its open interest was still relatively high at 1,131 lots -- or the equivalent of about 300,000 bags of coffee -- against certifiable coffee of 35,083 bags.
While London's direction hinges on New York, any new rally in London is likely to be short-lived as fundamentally, robustas are over supplied.
Technically, the market is running into layers of heavy resistance in place since the last major bull run in early 1996.
But May has to come down to at least $1,650 or $1,600 to confirm the downward reversal.
There were no fresh fundamental inputs but traders were keeping an eye on producers' talks due in London on March 22.

Indonesia, part of a six-member Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) technical group, said on Wednesday the grouping should consider the interest of consumers following the sharp hike in bean prices.

Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze reiterated that the grouping would abide by its decision to cut an extra 1.3 million bags of coffee in the first half of 1997. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
